title: Yara and the Bridge
premise: In 1899, Ivo Voss, indentured since childhood to the Meridian Trading Company on a pearl-lagoon colony, has survived by making himself unremarkable. When census taker Yara Okonkwo arrives to document the settlement before the century's end, her questions unravel the secret Ivo has guarded for ten years: his sister Ada, hidden among the company's laborers, is unregistered and therefore uncounted — and only registered persons may board the last berth of the repatriation ship leaving before the new colonial decree takes effect. As Ivo's silence and Yara's curiosity collide, he must decide whether to claim Ada at the cost of the found family of divers who raised him, or surrender the berth and his sister's future to protect them. In the end, Ivo registers Ada under the name of the dead diver Maren who raised them both, forfeiting his own passage — and Yara, moved by his sacrifice, falsifies the ledger a second time, registering Ivo as a free man, so that the new century begins with the family he chose, not the one the company owns.
about_author: Theo Okonkwo is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloging colonial trade ledgers from the pearl-lagoon settlements. Their fiction reimagines the unnamed laborers who appear in those records only as numbers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ten years after being indentured, Ivo dives the lagoon's shallow beds, counting pearls and silences in equal measure. He tends the memory of his mother's last words and keeps Ada's existence hidden even from his closest fellow diver, Tomas. The emotional beat: the cost of invisibility, worn like a second skin.

chapters.title: The Woman with the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Census taker Yara Okonkwo arrives at the company compound, brisk and observant, asking each laborer for names, births, kin. When her questions reach Ivo, one lands too close: 'Any siblings?' He lies, and watches her write the lie down. The beat: fear sharpened into a new kind of vigilance.

chapters.title: What Maren Left
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas recalls the night the dying diver Maren smuggled two children into the laborers' quarters, and how the divers became their unlikely family. Now he senses Ivo pulling away. The beat: found family rendered as inheritance — what the living owe the dead.

chapters.title: The Decree
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara learns the colonial office's new decree: unregistered persons will be classified as company property, and only registered individuals may claim berths on the final repatriation ship before the century turns. She suspects the Voss ledger is incomplete. The beat: duty beginning to chafe against conscience.

chapters.title: Ada in the Shallows
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo and Ada meet secretly at the reef; she begs him to register her before the decree lands. He calculates the risk and refuses — the company watches him too closely. Ada's fury cracks the silence he built to protect her. The beat: love curdling into resentment.

chapters.title: The Count That Doesn't Add
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Cross-checking ration ledgers against her census rolls, Yara finds a decade of small discrepancies — extra rice, a second pair of boots — all traced to Maren's old quarters. She confronts Ivo gently, offering not accusation but a door. The beat: the terrifying relief of being seen.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The company's overseer, Vell, announces the berth list will be posted in six days and warns Ivo that informants are rewarded. Ivo realizes Vell already suspects Ada exists and is baiting him. Tomas offers to take the blame if Ivo acts. The beat: rising dread; every ally becomes a liability.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara is ordered to certify the final registry, one name per berth, no amendments. She recognizes that helping Ivo would end her career and possibly her freedom. She spends a sleepless night with her own ledger, pen hovering. The beat: the climax's moral fulcrum, held in a bureaucrat's hand.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On registry day, Ivo declares Ada as Maren's daughter — his own name unspoken. Vell moves to seize them both, but Tomas and the divers stand as witnesses, and Yara, choosing conscience over career, certifies Ada's berth and quietly enters Ivo as a freedman. The beat: the sacrifice made, and answered.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing with Yara's. The ship departs with Ada aboard; Ivo stays on the shore he no longer hides on, among the family who raised him, as fireworks mark the new year. Yara leaves him her ledger as a gift — proof he existed. The beat: belonging redefined as a choice renewed daily.
